component.name: Kempt
component.summary: Tidy system updates for the Plasma desktop

description.p: Kempt is a Plasma 6 widget and a command-line tool for dnf and Flatpak updates. It shows which updates are pending, leaves out the ones you hold, and installs them from the panel.
The count in the panel comes from the same cache the update uses, so the two agree.

ul.li: dnf5 and Flatpak updates, with the version each package moves from and to.
Holds that skip a package but keep reporting it.
Offline staging for updates that could disturb the running session.

screenshot.caption: Kempt in the system tray, with the pending-updates popup open
The settings page: run surface, check interval, restart reminders and the password-prompt controls

description.p: An update run now says which dnf transaction it was, so it reports what it installed rather than everything that changed on the machine while it was going. A finished run no longer offers to stage what it has just staged. Each part of a run has a heading, flatpak end-of-life notices name the app that uses the runtime, and kempt doctor says when Discover's update notifier also starts with your session.

Flatpak runtimes are counted and listed, so the badge matches what an update really changes. A staged update can be discarded with kempt unstage, the popup says how old the package metadata behind its counts is, and a restart reports the transaction Kempt staged rather than whatever else ran.

A downloaded Fedora release upgrade is now protected by Kempt's root helper itself, so no other program running as you can cancel, discard or start it through Kempt without a password. Passwordless mode installs exactly the rule it checked, and only at its one fixed path.
The software center entry no longer names an icon of its own, and the installed documentation is limited to what someone using Kempt needs.

A machine a long way behind now updates: past about nine hundred pending packages the check used to fail and the panel blamed a missing installation. Kempt refuses to stage updates over a stored Fedora release upgrade, because staging would cancel the upgrade, and refuses to update an image-based Fedora, where rpm-ostree or bootc rather than dnf is what updates the system.

A hold added after an offline update was staged is no longer silent, in the command line or the popup. The panel widget is now its own package, kempt-plasmoid, so the command line no longer pulls in a desktop. Three ways a staged update could quietly stop being real are now caught and announced.
A widget installed before the CLI now walks you through installing the engine, with a Copy Commands button; kempt doctor catches a store copy shadowing the packaged widget.
